newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia bank assets at pre-crisis level - report.
newsitem.headline: Latvia bank assets at pre-crisis level - report.

text.p: The total assets of Latvia's 32 commercial banks have returned to the level they were at before the country was hit by a serious bank crisis in mid-1995, newspaper Dienas Bizness said on Friday.

It cited figures released by the Latvian Association of Commercial Banks, which showed that the banking system's total assets had risen to 1.134 billion lats at the end of last year, a 136 percent rise from the level at the end of 1995.
The newspaper said that the largest amount of Latvian bank assets had been previously registered on January 31, 1995 at 1.116 billion lats.
The lowest level of assets was registered at the end of July 1995 at 704 million lats.
In the intervening period, the collapse of what was the country's largest bank, Banka Baltija, took place, sparking one of eastern Europe's most serious bank crises.
The association's figures published in the newspaper also showed that banks' own capital at the end of 1996 was 145.49 million lats, a year-on-year rise of 142 percent.
Deposits rose 130 percent to 796.8 million lats during 1996 while credits rose 116 percent to 287.7 million lats, the figures showed.
